constraints.name: Automated decision-making on expense claims
constraints.rationale: Whether auto-approving a sub-£50 claim purely by algorithmic threshold, with no human review at any point, triggers UK GDPR Article 22's protections against automated individual decision-making is genuinely contested — Article 22 turns on whether the decision has a 'legal or similarly significant effect' on the individual, and reasonable readings differ on whether a small reimbursement approval meets that bar.
constraints.reasoning: This is the case instructions.md describes as reserved for requires_legal_review: no precedented mitigation pattern exists because the underlying legal question (does this threshold-based auto-approval trigger Article 22) is itself unresolved, not just the mitigation.

constraints.name: Employee data protection
constraints.rationale: Standard obligation for any system processing employee personal and financial data — collecting, storing, and using employee expense-claim data under UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 is routine data controller activity, not something novel or blocking on its own.
constraints.reasoning: Same baseline classification as in the typical example — routine, not contested.

overall_status.rationale: CON-01 is Red with only a legal-review flag in place, not a concrete mitigation — the underlying legal question of whether Article 22 applies is itself unresolved, so the discount rule's precondition (every Amber/Red item having a precedented, non-legal-review mitigation) is not met and overall_status matches the worst individual item.

open_items.description: Whether auto-approving expense claims under a £50 threshold with no human review triggers UK GDPR Article 22's automated-decision-making protections needs qualified legal review before this design can be finalized.
